documentedAliases.text: • The variety of living things found in a region is called its biodiversity. Even anordinary place has much more of it than a quick look suggests.

documentedAliases.text: • Grouping means arranging things by the features they share. Different rulesanswer different questions; each must be applied consistently.

documentedAliases.text: • Woody stems and branching help distinguish trees and shrubs from non-woodyherbs. Climbing and trailing describe growth habits, which can overlap with thesedescriptions.

documentedAliases.text: • The pattern of veins in a leaf is called venation. Two common patterns arereticulate and parallel.

documentedAliases.text: • Two common root systems are taproot and fibrous root systems. A taproot has onemain root. Fibrous roots form a spreading bunch.

documentedAliases.text: • Among flowering plants, dicots have two cotyledons and monocots have one.

documentedAliases.text: • These three features go together. Dicots generally have reticulate venation and ataproot. Monocots generally have parallel venation and fibrous roots. Theseassociations support predictions that must be checked.

documentedAliases.text: People across India eat widely different food, and the difference is not random. Itfollows the crops that grow in each region, which follow soil and climate, and is thenshaped by culture, religion and taste.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: Culinary practices have changed sharply within living memory — from chulha to gasstove, from sil-batta to mixer-grinder — driven by new technology, better transportand faster communication. The changes brought real gains and some real losses.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and minerals are nutrient groups studiedhere. Water is also an essential nutrient. Food supplies dietary fibre as well.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Carbohydrates and fats supply energy and are called energy-giving foods. Fatcarries more energy per gram than carbohydrate and is the body's store.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Proteins build and repair the body and are called body-building foods. Growingchildren and athletes need proportionally more.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Lack of a nutrient can cause a deficiency disorder. Symptoms can also have othercauses, so medical assessment matters. Examples include Vitamin C deficiencycausing scurvy and iodine deficiency contributing to goitre.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Dietary fibre resists digestion by our own enzymes; gut microbes can break downsome of it. Fibre helps bowel function. Water transports dissolved substances andhelps regulate body temperature.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Starch, fat and protein can be detected with simple tests: iodine turns starchblue-black, fat leaves a translucent oily patch on paper, and copper sulfate withcaustic soda turns protein violet. Most foods contain more than one nutrient.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: A balanced diet supplies all the nutrients a particular person needs, in the rightamounts, with enough roughage and water. What is balanced depends on age, sex,activity, health and way of life.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Junk foods carry plenty of energy from sugar and fat and little else. Millets arecalled nutri-cereals because they carry fibre and minerals along with theircarbohydrate, and they grow on less water.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.

documentedAliases.text: • Food miles measures distance, not total environmental impact. Transport method,farming and storage also matter. Wasted food wastes resources used to produce it.
documentedAliases.reason: Approved-format recap edit: concise restatement of the same concepts; complete original teaching explanations remain in the lesson. Chapter 3 also replaces overgeneralised food claims with qualified statements.
